BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against the Buyer Playbook

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material term. Several positions would need Amelia Frost's written authority to accept, and none has been given. The draft's "[STANDARD]" tags, "FINAL" label and "reviewer efficiency note" do not bind us. I have reviewed every clause, not only the items marked [OPEN]. Nothing in the package should be treated as agreed.

## 1. Departures from the playbook

| Area | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m (20% only as conditional fallback with Frost's written authority) | Reject. No authority given. |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. Five times our figure. |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, deductible (excess only) | AUD 50,000, tipping (first dollar once exceeded) | Reject. Five times the basket, and the deductible structure removes recovery on the first AUD 250k. |
| General claims period | 18 months | 24 months (18 only with Frost approval) | Reject. |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject. Core structural departure. |
| Limitations/reliance | Apply to all claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of everything | Reject. Non-waivable. |
| Disclosure | Whole data room (DL 1.1), public registers and Accounts (DL 1.2), general disclosure | Specific fair disclosure only | Reject. |
| Buyer knowledge | Blanket exclusion, including matters discoverable from data room or public records | Delete; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry | Reject. |
| Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery | Effective consent and evidence of conditions before Completion | Reject. ~AUD 3.6m revenue (~30%); DL 2 confirms no final consent. |
| Riverlark | Release "following Completion" | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases | Reject. ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; DL 3 confirms not repaid. |
| Bonuses (DD-005) | Not itemised in funds flow | Specific line item or seller-funded, including on-costs | Reject. AUD 420k plus on-costs unaddressed; DL 5 confirms this. |
| Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment, "adequate" | Broaden; preserve SOW3 cure | Reject. AUD 180k open per DD-010, unverified. |
| DD-006 incident | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; no assumption either way | Do not accept the characterisation. |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary course" | Assess; no automatic debt or price treatment | Do not accept without the contracts. |
| Tax/IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain OPEN; no unlimited liability; no hidden general-regime override | Reject. |
| Title | DD-012 share register as sole evidence | Independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence | Reject. The register is an internal source, not independent proof. |

## 2. Reasoning on the material issues

**a) Fundamental and title claims.** The Seller wants capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits. This is the most serious structural issue. Title is the core of what we are buying. Under the Seller's draft, a title defect could be capped at AUD 4.8m and expire at 18 months. Our playbook requires a separate regime, and the Seller's clause-wide cross-application ("any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims") would override it. Any drafting that pulls title into the general regime should be struck.

**b) Disclosure and buyer knowledge together.** The combination is the most dangerous part of the package. DL 1.1 and 1.2 disclose the entire data room and public registers. Clause 8.3 then bars claims for anything discoverable there. Together they would defeat most warranty claims, since almost any problem is somewhere in a data room or register. Specific disclosure only, and no blanket knowledge bar, should be non-negotiable.

**c) Conditions and consents.** Bluefen and Riverlark are both material and both unresolved on the Seller's own disclosure. Treating Bluefen consent as satisfied on delivery, and deferring the Riverlark release until after Completion, would move risk to us at the point we have least leverage. The playbook requires both to be resolved before Completion. Our position should be that Completion is not to occur until these are satisfied, or that the price and funds flow are adjusted to reflect them.

**d) Funds flow.** The AUD 420k bonuses are missing from the funds flow. The Seller's draft leaves on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) unaddressed (DL 5). Our position: a specific line item in the funds flow, or Seller funding. Silent exclusion is not acceptable. Confirm the on-cost calculation with tax advisers.

**e) Ironquay.** The indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. The AUD 180k figure is unverified in either direction. We should broaden the indemnity to cover all Ironquay IP and related claims, keep the SOW3 cure, and require payment evidence before Completion.

**f) DD-006 incident.** The Seller's description ("not expected to be material") is a view, not a finding. The record does not establish whether there was unauthorised access, what the exact scope is, or whether notification is required. Exposure involves approximately 1,240 records containing personal information. We should not assume a breach, but we should require log preservation, an investigation with a defined scope and timetable, regular updates, and privacy-counsel input on notification obligations. Whether to seek a specific indemnity is a negotiation decision for the deal team. It is not a playbook requirement, and I would not assume it has been decided.

**g) Title evidence.** DD-012 is the Seller's own register. The playbook requires independent evidence: an ASIC company extract, a PPSR and encumbrance search, the share transfer or certificate chain, and evidence of Seller authority. DL 10 confirms the Buyer has not completed its own verification.

**h) Tax and IP.** The Seller's view that these are settled under the general regime is rejected. Both remain open. The Seller's position that tax and IP warranties fall under the general cap would imply limited liability, which is not acceptable.

**i) Items not covered by the playbook.** The office lease (DD-007) and the Mossvale assignment restriction (DD-009) are disclosed in DL 7 and DL 9, but the disclosures expressly decline to say whether landlord or Mossvale consent is required. We should not accept that gap. Request written confirmation from the Seller on whether consent is required, and treat any "yes" as a new consent item for the Completion checklist.

**j) Process.** The "FINAL," "settled at principal level" and "not to be re-opened" claims are the Seller's assertions. We have not agreed them. Only Amelia Frost can authorise departures from the playbook, and no such authority is recorded. The market-context paragraph is also not binding. Our playbook is the instruction.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the package as drafted.** Respond with our mark-up and state that no [STANDARD] or FINAL designation is accepted.
2. **Caps and thresholds:** 25% / AUD 6m general cap; AUD 5k de minimis; AUD 50k tipping basket. Hold the 20% fallback until Amelia Frost gives written authority identifying the draft.
3. **Time limits:** 24 months general; no cross-application to other regimes.
4. **Title and fundamentals:** separate regime, 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Strike the cross-application language.
5. **Fraud and deliberate misconduct:** carve out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum enforceable extent. Non-waivable.
6. **Disclosure:** specific fair disclosure only. Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2 whole-data-room, register and Accounts disclosure.
7. **Buyer knowledge:** delete clause 8.3. Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
8. **Bluefen:** effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions before Completion. No consent-on-delivery or reasonable-endeavours-only standard.
9. **Riverlark:** current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
10. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item, or Seller-funded.
11. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, keep the SOW3 cure, and require payment evidence for the AUD 180k.
12. **DD-006:** require log preservation, a scoped investigation, updates and privacy-counsel input. Assume no confirmed breach or quantified loss in either direction.
13. **Sandbar renewals:** request contracts and assess. Do not reclassify as debt or deduct from price automatically.
14. **Tax and IP:** keep open. Reject the "settled under the general regime" position.
15. **Title:** require independent searches and evidence of Seller authority. DD-012 is not sufficient.
16. **Lease and Mossvale:** obtain written Seller confirmation on whether consent is required.
17. **Governance:** brief Amelia Frost on the departures before any concession. Any movement from the playbook requires her written authority identifying the draft.

*Please have NSW counsel confirm the enforceability of the fraud carve-out and the drafting of the limitation regime, and have privacy counsel assess the DD-006 notification position.*
